title: Fix hotpatch path selection causing resolver mismatch in multiregion peering
creator: Lena Kim
description: Several customers on Dedicated saw intermittent DNS resolution failures and asymmetric egress selection after the 2026-02-18 dataplane hotpatch. Symptoms included tenant-resolver affinity flip, resolved names appearing to belong to another tenant, and transient 502s from origin in peered regions. This ticket tracks the production fix, postmortem items, and longer-term safeguards.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a Dedicated tenant with multiregion VPC peering configured (us-west + eu-west). 2) Provision a long-running model endpoint on dedicated GPU pool in us-west. 3) Trigger scale-up event on the pool causing dataplane host rebind. 4) Send sustained DNS lookups and outbound requests via the endpoint while peering resync occurs. 5) Observe resolver selection flip in netflow logs and mismatched DNS answers in resolver-audit logs.
impact: Multiple enterprise customers experienced intermittent request misrouting and stale resolver answers for 6-18 minutes during peering handovers. This caused higher client-side error rates, support escalations (SUP-98321, SUP-98702), and increased costs as retry storms hit fallback endpoints.
mitigation: 1) Emergency rollback of the hotpatch to previous control-plane release for affected clusters (completed 2026-02-20). 2) Applied a temporary sticky binding on egress resolver selection for existing flows to avoid mid-flight flips. 3) Added detection alerts to PagerDuty channel for resolver-affinity-entropy metric.
root_cause: The new hotpatch introduced a reorder in route-install paths that caused a small window where the control plane updated route preferences without atomically reconciling per-tenant egress resolver bindings. When a scale or peering event coincided with ephemeral NAT reallocation, some hosts reselected resolvers based on fresh route state, losing their prior affinity. This exposed a race between route reconciliation and resolver-binding reconciliation.
resolution: Implemented an atomic reconcile in the route-applier that gates resolver binding changes until routes are fully committed. Added idempotent egress-binding marker to the control plane to prevent double-assignment during concurrent topology updates. Patch landed in PR #4102 and rolled out to affected clusters on 2026-03-03.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary rollout to non-critical us-west clusters (2026-03-03). 2) Expand to all Dedicated us-west clusters (2026-03-05). 3) Monitor resolver-affinity-entropy and tenant-dns-mismatch dashboards for 72 hours. 4) Full global rollout (including eu-west peering) after 72h stable window (target 2026-03-10). 5) Backfill unit + e2e tests to prevent regressions.
